title: Frame-by-frame and onion skinning
summary: Draw a bouncing ball one keyframe at a time with F6 and F7, use onion skinning to see the frames around the one you draw, step through it, and play it on a loop.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
In this lesson you will animate a ball bouncing across the stage by drawing it again on each frame, the way hand-drawn animation is made.

The new document runs at 12 frames per second, so each drawing stays up a little longer.

steps.title: Pick the Oval tool
steps.text: Press O, or choose the Oval tool from the Rectangle slot.

steps.title: Frame 1: the ball up high
steps.text: Hold Shift and draw a ball near the top left of the stage. This is the top of its fall.

steps.title: Go to frame 2
steps.text: Click the cell under frame 2 in the timeline.

steps.title: A blank keyframe
steps.text: Press F7, or choose Insert > Timeline > Blank Keyframe. Frame 2 is now a keyframe of its own, with nothing on it: the stage is empty.

steps.title: Turn on onion skinning
steps.text: Click this button, or press Alt+Shift+O. The ball from frame 1 shows faintly, so you can place the next drawing against it. Frames before the playhead show in blue, frames after it in green.

steps.title: Frame 2: falling
steps.text: Draw the ball again, lower down and a little to the right of the faint one.

steps.title: Go to frame 3
steps.text: Click the cell under frame 3.

steps.title: A keyframe with a copy
steps.text: This time press F6, or choose Insert > Timeline > Keyframe. A keyframe starts with a copy of the frame before it, so the ball is already there to move.

steps.title: Pick the Selection tool
steps.text: Press V.

steps.title: Frame 3: hitting the ground
steps.text: Double-click the ball to select its fill and outline, then drag it down to the bottom of the stage, a little further right.

steps.title: Squash it (if you like)
steps.text:
A ball squashes as it lands. Press Q for the Free Transform tool and drag the handles to make the ball a little wider and shorter.

Click Next when you are happy with it.

steps.title: Frame 4: bouncing up
steps.text: Click the cell under frame 4, then press F7 for a blank keyframe, so you can draw the ball fresh.

steps.title: Draw the rising ball
steps.text: Press O and draw the ball rising again, up and to the right of where it landed. The onion skin shows the frames before it.

steps.title: Frame 5: up high again
steps.text: Click the cell under frame 5 and press F7.

steps.title: Draw the top of the bounce
steps.text: Draw the ball near the top of the stage, further right again.

steps.title: The onion skin markers
steps.text: The markers in the ruler above the frames show which frames the onion skin covers, a few each side of the playhead. Drag a marker to show more frames or fewer. Right-click the onion skin button for more settings.

steps.title: Back to the start
steps.text: Click the Step back button, or press , (comma), until the playhead is on frame 1.

steps.title: Step through the drawings
steps.text:
Now step forward with this button, or . (period), to frame 3. Flipping between drawings like this is the best way to check the motion.

Alt+. and Alt+, jump to the next and previous keyframe.

steps.title: Loop playback
steps.text: Click the Loop button, or press Alt+Shift+L, so playback goes round and round. Drag the ends of the loop range in the ruler to loop only part of the timeline.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click Play. Turn the onion skin off to see the ball move cleanly. Press Enter again to stop.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You drew an animation frame by frame, with F7 for empty keyframes and F6 for copies, checked it with onion skinning and stepping, and played it on a loop.

To keep the ball bouncing, add more keyframes after frame 5. Then try Symbols and editing in place.
